cover.title: The bond market just hit a [[24-YEAR]] high

slides.label: Treasury yields
slides.body: The government borrows by selling bonds. The yield is the interest it pays. The 10-year topped [[5.3%]] in October, the highest since 2002.

slides.label: How high it went
slides.body: The US 30-year yield hit [[5.59%]] on Sept 29, the highest since 2002. The UK 30-year gilt passed [[6%]] on Oct 1.

slides.label: Why it happened
slides.body: Oil spiked above [[$100]] on Iran supply fears. Inflation worries grew, bond prices fell, and yields rose.

slides.label: This week
slides.body: The 10-year yield slid below [[green|5%]] to [[green|4.90%]] as a tech selloff sent money into Treasuries.

caption:
The bond market just hit its highest yields in 24 years. 📈

The US 30-year hit 5.59% on Sept 29, the highest since 2002. This week the 10-year slid back below 5%.
